subject: strategies/portfolio
hypothesis: The 3-strategy portfolio (trend-following, mean-reversion, ORB) with ATR/structure stops is net profitable on real historical daily data
method: full-history backtest, ATM strike, 7-day expiry, one conceptual unit
notes: Positive in-sample total P&L on all three, but no OOS split, no costs/slippage/lot-sizing - informational only.

subject: strategies/portfolio
hypothesis: Run 001R's positive total P&L is consistent across independent time periods, not concentrated in one lucky stretch
method: 5-fold walk-forward, 5-bar embargo gap, independent per-fold backtest
notes: High variance relative to mean on all three - not a consistent edge fold-to-fold.

subject: strategies/portfolio
hypothesis: Run 001R's total P&L is statistically distinguishable from zero given the actual trade-level distribution
method: bootstrap resampling (20,000 resamples) of trade P&Ls for a 90% CI on total P&L
notes: 90% CIs exclude zero on all three, but this conflicts with run-002r's fold-level inconsistency - suggestive, not proof, given no OOS holdout and non-independent instruments.

subject: strategies/trend_following
hypothesis: The most recent walk-forward fold's losses are explained by a specific, identifiable market mechanism rather than random noise
method: attribution breakdown by strategy and entry_regime, cross-checked against real price data

metrics.mechanism: trend-following whipsaw at a Nov 2025-Mar 2026 market reversal

notes: Confirmed mechanism (real market reversal), but deliberately NOT acted on with a new filter - would be fitting a rule to the one reversal event in this dataset.

subject: strategies/contract_selection
hypothesis: Selecting strikes by capital efficiency (delta/premium) instead of always ATM improves backtest P&L and drawdown
method: A/B comparison, same full-history backtest with use_contract_selector True vs False
notes: Modest improvement on all three, in-sample only - plausible and mechanistically sensible but not validated; default kept at ATM-only.
